title: Friend count per user
context: Friendships are stored once (user_a < user_b); count both directions.
task: Return user_id and friends = number of friendships the user appears in (either column), for users with at least one friend.
hint: UNION ALL both directions, then GROUP BY.
answer: SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) AS friends FROM (SELECT user_a AS user_id FROM friendships UNION ALL SELECT user_b FROM friendships) GROUP BY user_id;

title: Users with no friends
context: Isolated accounts for the 'people you may know' push.
task: Return user_id and name for users who appear in neither user_a nor user_b.
hint: NOT IN / NOT EXISTS against both columns.
answer: SELECT u.user_id, u.name FROM users u WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM friendships f WHERE f.user_a = u.user_id OR f.user_b = u.user_id);

title: Most connected users
task: Return user_id, name and friends for the top 3 users by friend count (ties by user_id).
answer: WITH d AS (SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) AS friends FROM (SELECT user_a AS user_id FROM friendships UNION ALL SELECT user_b FROM friendships) GROUP BY user_id) SELECT d.user_id, u.name, d.friends FROM d JOIN users u ON u.user_id = d.user_id ORDER BY d.friends DESC, d.user_id LIMIT 3;

title: Friends of user 3
context: Normalise the undirected edge into a friend list.
task: Return friend_id for every friend of user 3, ordered ascending.
hint: CASE WHEN user_a = 3 THEN user_b ELSE user_a END.
answer: SELECT CASE WHEN user_a = 3 THEN user_b ELSE user_a END AS friend_id FROM friendships WHERE user_a = 3 OR user_b = 3 ORDER BY friend_id;

title: Mutual friends of users 1 and 2
task: Return friend_id for users who are friends with both user 1 and user 2.
hint: INTERSECT of two normalised friend lists.
answer: SELECT CASE WHEN user_a = 1 THEN user_b ELSE user_a END AS friend_id FROM friendships WHERE 1 IN (user_a, user_b) INTERSECT SELECT CASE WHEN user_a = 2 THEN user_b ELSE user_a END FROM friendships WHERE 2 IN (user_a, user_b);

title: Friends of friends of user 1
context: Second-degree connections, excluding user 1 and their direct friends.
task: Return DISTINCT fof_id = users who are friends with any friend of user 1, but are not user 1 and not a direct friend.
hint: Build a normalised edge list CTE (both directions) and join it to itself.
answer: WITH e AS (SELECT user_a AS u, user_b AS v FROM friendships UNION ALL SELECT user_b, user_a FROM friendships), f1 AS (SELECT v FROM e WHERE u = 1) SELECT DISTINCT e.v AS fof_id FROM e JOIN f1 ON f1.v = e.u WHERE e.v <> 1 AND e.v NOT IN (SELECT v FROM f1);

title: Duplicate or reversed edges
context: Every friendship should be stored once with user_a < user_b.
task: Return friendship_id where user_a >= user_b (bad rows).
answer: SELECT friendship_id FROM friendships WHERE user_a >= user_b;

title: Friend pairs from the same country
task: Return same_country_pct (1 dp) = friendships where both users share a country / all friendships * 100.
answer: SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN a.country = b.country THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) * 100, 1) AS same_country_pct FROM friendships f JOIN users a ON a.user_id = f.user_a JOIN users b ON b.user_id = f.user_b;

title: Age gap between friends
task: Return user_a, user_b and age_gap = ABS(age difference) for friendships with a gap of 20 or more years.
answer: SELECT f.user_a, f.user_b, ABS(a.age - b.age) AS age_gap FROM friendships f JOIN users a ON a.user_id = f.user_a JOIN users b ON b.user_id = f.user_b WHERE ABS(a.age - b.age) >= 20;

title: Engagement rate per platform
context: Which app engages more per view?
task: Return platform and engagement_pct (2 dp) = SUM(likes + comments + shares) * 100.0 / SUM(reach).
answer: SELECT platform, ROUND(SUM(likes + comments + shares) * 100.0 / SUM(reach), 2) AS engagement_pct FROM posts GROUP BY platform;

title: Creator vs non-creator reach
task: Return is_creator and avg_reach (1 dp) per group.
answer: SELECT u.is_creator, ROUND(AVG(p.reach), 1) AS avg_reach FROM posts p JOIN users u ON u.user_id = p.user_id GROUP BY u.is_creator;

title: Reactions on own posts
context: Users reacting to their own content.
task: Return reaction_id, user_id and post_id where the reactor is the post's author.
answer: SELECT r.reaction_id, r.user_id, r.post_id FROM reactions r JOIN posts p ON p.post_id = r.post_id WHERE r.user_id = p.user_id;

title: Posts with zero reactions
context: Content that got no explicit reaction rows.
task: Return post_id and user_id for posts with no rows in reactions.
answer: SELECT p.post_id, p.user_id FROM posts p LEFT JOIN reactions r ON r.post_id = p.post_id WHERE r.reaction_id IS NULL;

title: Users who never posted
task: Return user_id and name for users with no posts.
answer: SELECT u.user_id, u.name FROM users u LEFT JOIN posts p ON p.user_id = u.user_id WHERE p.post_id IS NULL;

title: Every user's post count
task: Return user_id and posts = COUNT(post_id) for every user.
answer: SELECT u.user_id, COUNT(p.post_id) AS posts FROM users u LEFT JOIN posts p ON p.user_id = u.user_id GROUP BY u.user_id;

title: Posts above the platform average likes
task: Return post_id, platform and likes where likes > the average likes on that platform.
answer: SELECT p.post_id, p.platform, p.likes FROM posts p WHERE p.likes > (SELECT AVG(likes) FROM posts WHERE platform = p.platform);

title: Users who reacted to a friend's post
task: Return DISTINCT user_id (reactor) for reactions on posts whose author is a friend of the reactor.
answer: WITH e AS (SELECT user_a AS u, user_b AS v FROM friendships UNION ALL SELECT user_b, user_a FROM friendships) SELECT DISTINCT r.user_id FROM reactions r JOIN posts p ON p.post_id = r.post_id WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM e WHERE e.u = r.user_id AND e.v = p.user_id);

title: Creators with no reactions at all
context: Creators whose posts never got a reaction row.
task: Return user_id for creators (is_creator = 1) with at least one post and no reactions on any post.
hint: EXISTS on posts, NOT EXISTS on reactions via posts.
answer: SELECT u.user_id FROM users u WHERE u.is_creator = 1 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM posts p WHERE p.user_id = u.user_id) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM reactions r JOIN posts p ON p.post_id = r.post_id WHERE p.user_id = u.user_id);

title: Reaction sentiment per post
context: Positive (like, love, haha, wow) vs negative (sad, angry).
task: Return post_id, positive and negative counts for posts with at least one reaction.
answer: SELECT post_id, SUM(CASE WHEN reaction IN ('like','love','haha','wow') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS positive, SUM(CASE WHEN reaction IN ('sad','angry') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS negative FROM reactions GROUP BY post_id;

title: Post type mix per platform, wide
task: Return platform, photo, video, text, reel = post counts.
answer: SELECT platform, SUM(CASE WHEN post_type = 'photo' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS photo, SUM(CASE WHEN post_type = 'video' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS video, SUM(CASE WHEN post_type = 'text' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS text, SUM(CASE WHEN post_type = 'reel' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS reel FROM posts GROUP BY platform;

title: Friendships formed per year
task: Return year (integer) and friendships count.
answer: SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y', created_at) AS INTEGER) AS year, COUNT(*) AS friendships FROM friendships GROUP BY year;

title: Days to first post
task: Return user_id and days_to_first_post (integer) for users with posts.
answer: SELECT u.user_id, CAST(julianday(MIN(p.post_date)) - julianday(u.signup_date) AS INTEGER) AS days_to_first_post FROM users u JOIN posts p ON p.user_id = u.user_id GROUP BY u.user_id;

title: Reaction lag
context: Average days between post and reaction.
task: Return avg_lag_days (2 dp) = average of julianday(reacted_at) − julianday(post_date).
answer: SELECT ROUND(AVG(julianday(r.reacted_at) - julianday(p.post_date)), 2) AS avg_lag_days FROM reactions r JOIN posts p ON p.post_id = r.post_id;

title: Weekend posting share
context: Do people post more at weekends?
task: Return weekend_pct (1 dp) = posts on Sat/Sun / all posts * 100.
answer: SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN strftime('%w', post_date) IN ('0','6') THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) * 100, 1) AS weekend_pct FROM posts;

title: Share of reach by post type
task: Return post_type and share_pct (1 dp) = type reach / total reach * 100.
hint: CTE then divide by the CTE total.
answer: WITH t AS (SELECT post_type, SUM(reach) AS reach FROM posts GROUP BY post_type) SELECT post_type, ROUND(reach * 100.0 / (SELECT SUM(reach) FROM t), 1) AS share_pct FROM t;

title: Conversion rate and CPA
task: Return advertiser, cvr_pct (2 dp) = conversions * 100.0 / clicks and cpa (2 dp) = spend * 1.0 / conversions for campaigns with conversions > 0.
answer: SELECT advertiser, ROUND(conversions * 100.0 / clicks, 2) AS cvr_pct, ROUND(spend * 1.0 / conversions, 2) AS cpa FROM ad_campaigns WHERE conversions > 0;

title: Best CPA per vertical
context: Category winners on cost per acquisition.
task: Return vertical, advertiser and cpa (2 dp) for the campaign with the lowest CPA in each vertical (conversions > 0; ties by advertiser).
hint: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY vertical ORDER BY cpa).
answer: SELECT vertical, advertiser, ROUND(cpa, 2) AS cpa FROM (SELECT vertical, advertiser, spend * 1.0 / conversions AS cpa, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY vertical ORDER BY spend * 1.0 / conversions, advertiser) AS rn FROM ad_campaigns WHERE conversions > 0) WHERE rn = 1;

title: Audience match
context: How many users fall into each campaign's age_target?
task: Return advertiser, age_target and eligible_users = users in that bracket ('18-24' → 18–24, '25-34', '35-44', 'all' → everyone).
answer: SELECT c.advertiser, c.age_target, COUNT(u.user_id) AS eligible_users FROM ad_campaigns c JOIN users u ON (c.age_target = 'all') OR (c.age_target = '18-24' AND u.age BETWEEN 18 AND 24) OR (c.age_target = '25-34' AND u.age BETWEEN 25 AND 34) OR (c.age_target = '35-44' AND u.age BETWEEN 35 AND 44) GROUP BY c.campaign_id;

title: Viral posts
context: Shares above 10% of likes and reach over 10,000.
task: Return post_id, reach, likes and shares where shares > 0.1 × likes and reach > 10000.
answer: SELECT post_id, reach, likes, shares FROM posts WHERE shares > 0.1 * likes AND reach > 10000;

title: Cross-platform posters
task: Return user_id and platforms = COUNT(DISTINCT platform) for users posting on 2 or more platforms.
answer: SELECT user_id, COUNT(DISTINCT platform) AS platforms FROM posts GROUP BY user_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT platform) >= 2;

title: Reactors who never post
task: Return user_id values that appear in reactions but not in posts.
answer: SELECT user_id FROM reactions EXCEPT SELECT user_id FROM posts;

title: Impossible engagement
context: likes + comments + shares can't exceed reach.
task: Return post_id, reach and total_engagement where likes + comments + shares > reach.
answer: SELECT post_id, reach, likes + comments + shares AS total_engagement FROM posts WHERE likes + comments + shares > reach;

title: Reactions before the post existed
task: Return reaction_id, reacted_at and post_date where reacted_at < post_date.
answer: SELECT r.reaction_id, r.reacted_at, p.post_date FROM reactions r JOIN posts p ON p.post_id = r.post_id WHERE r.reacted_at < p.post_date;
